title: question
description: One entry in the 3-tier ask-a-human question queue (spec Part B). Standardized, one-question-per-entry shape so a question is never a free-text ping -- it always carries pre-researched options, a recommendation, and the exact fallback assumption a Tier-2 (safe-to-assume) case logs and continues with. Produced/consumed only by dv_harness/question_queue.py -- never hand-authored.

id.description: Q-ID. Domain-prefixed (matches `domain`, upper-cased) plus an 8-hex-char stable digest of `question_key`, so the SAME question asked twice mints the SAME id rather than a fresh one.

question_key.description: Stable dedup key for this exact question, independent of `id`'s derived hex -- what `dv_harness.question_queue`'s repeat-question-rate metric and decisions.md persistence are keyed on. Two asks with the same question_key are the SAME question; once a HUMAN has answered it, every later ask must self-resolve at Tier 1 from that persisted decision, never re-escalate. A persisted Tier-2 auto-assumption does NOT confer that -- it is the harness's own provisional guess, so a later ask of the same key that trips a Tier-3 hard trigger still escalates for real (see classify_tier's evaluation order).

blocking.description: true iff tier == 3 (Cannot-Assume): the harness stops and waits for a human answer. false for tier == 1 (already self-resolved, nothing to wait on) or tier == 2 (Safe-to-Assume: logged and continued automatically, never blocks). The tier-3 half of this is MACHINE-ENFORCED by the allOf block below -- see its own comment for why prose alone was not enough.

domain.description: vip: VIP configuration/behavior question -- routes to owner DV-owner/Synopsys-AE. dut: DUT RTL/port/register question -- routes to owner designer. env: environment/component-hierarchy/config_db question -- routes to owner DV-owner. Routing is a literal table (dv_harness.question_queue.route_owner), never inferred per-question.

owner.description: Must equal route_owner(domain) -- see the allOf block below, which pins the exact literal value per domain.

context_path.description: Where in the real evidence (e.g. an env.manifest.json JSON-pointer path, a file:line, a register/port name) this question concerns -- never a vague restatement of the question text itself.

options.description: 2-3 PRE-RESEARCHED options -- never an open-ended free-text question. Each option must already be a real, evaluated possibility, not a placeholder the human has to invent from scratch. This object form is the single PERSISTED shape; callers may also hand add_question() a plain ["option a", "option b"] list, which question_queue.normalize_options() coerces to this shape at the door. That asymmetry is deliberate: accepting bare strings HERE would force every reader of a stored record (validate_question's recommendation-in-labels cross-check, decisions.md rendering, digest batching) to branch per element forever, to buy an input convenience that costs nothing to absorb once on the way in.

rationale.description: Why this option is plausible -- the pre-research evidence, one sentence.

recommendation.description: Must equal one of options[].label -- dv_harness.question_queue.validate_question() checks this structurally (JSON Schema alone cannot cross-reference array values).

assumption_if_unanswered.description: The exact assumption a Tier-2 (safe-to-assume) classification logs and proceeds with. Required on every question, even a Tier-3 one that will never silently use it, so a later relaxation of this question's tier never leaves the assumption undefined.

tier.description: 1 = Self-resolve (answered from env.manifest.json/MCP or a persisted prior decision -- no human involved). 2 = Safe-to-assume (logged, continues; worst case is one wasted, cheaply-detected, cheaply-rerun regression). 3 = Cannot-assume (hard-coded trigger: affects pass/fail verdict, spec intent, or whether a read-only file should change -- stop and escalate).

tier_reason.description: Which classify_tier() rule fired -- e.g. 'decisions_store_hit', 'hard_trigger:affects_pass_fail_verdict', 'no_hard_trigger_low_blast_radius'. Never blank -- a tier is never assigned by unrecorded judgment.

status.description: OPEN: tier 3, awaiting a human answer (blocking). SELF_RESOLVED: tier 1, answer came from a persisted decision or the manifest at ask time. ASSUMED: tier 2, assumption_if_unanswered was logged and execution continued. ANSWERED: a human has since supplied a real answer (via `answer`), whether this question started OPEN or ASSUMED.

basis.description: The evidence/reasoning basis for `answer` -- required alongside any non-null answer.

overturned.description: true iff this question's answer replaced an earlier Tier-2 auto-assumption with a genuinely different value -- feeds the assumption-overturned-rate metric.

resolved_from_decision_id.description: For a SELF_RESOLVED (tier 1) question: the id of the prior question whose persisted decision supplied this answer.

allOf.$comment: tier 3 => blocking true. Added 2026-09-03 after a review proved a hand-built {tier:3, blocking:false, status:'SELF_RESOLVED'} record passed validate_question() cleanly: `blocking`'s own description already said 'true iff tier == 3', but a description is not a constraint, so nothing stopped a non-blocking Tier-3 record -- a cannot-assume question that never stops for a human -- from being persisted as valid. The rule is one-directional on purpose: tier 3 pins blocking to true, while tier 1/2 are left to the `blocking` boolean itself rather than being pinned to false here, so this constraint only ever adds escalation and can never suppress it.
